extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and patent applicants interacting with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of USPTO/MPEP procedural and substantive standards for preparing, filing, and examining U.S. patent applications (formatting, drawings, claims, deposits, declarations, representation, conduct, and related procedural requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Application: To contain but one invention unless connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should claim only a single invention unless multiple inventions are connected in such a manner that they properly belong in the same application (see 1.141).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by patent practitioner for juristic entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be represented by a patent practitioner if juristic entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities (juristic persons) are required to have a registered patent practitioner represent them in USPTO proceedings (see 1.31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct with decorum and courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: Required to conduct business with decorum and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties, attorneys, and agents transacting business with the Office must maintain professional decorum and courtesy; discourteous communications may not be entered (see 1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to report assistance received
rubrics_metrics.description: Required to report assistance received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/representatives must disclose assistance received in preparing or prosecuting applications as required by Office practice (see 1.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address and inventor residence data
rubrics_metrics.description: Mailing address and residence of inventors may be provided in oath/declaration or in application data sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor contact/residence information can be supplied either in the oath/declaration or on the application data sheet (see 1.63, 1.76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness before examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are examined only when complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application will be examined by the Office only when it meets the completeness requirements (see 1.53 and related pre-AIA guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering and form requirements for claims and paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbering of claims and numbering of paragraphs must follow Office practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims and specification paragraphs must be numbered in accordance with the Office formatting rules (see 1.52, 1.75, 1.126, 1.125). Claims commence on a separate sheet or electronic page per formatting rules (see 1.52(b)(3), 1.75(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must conform to invention and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must conform to the invention and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim language and scope must be supported by and consistent with the disclosed invention and the specification; claims not so supported are objectionable or subject to rejection (see 1.75(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims form: dependent, multiple dependent, and dependent form allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be in dependent form; multiple dependent claims are permitted; dependent claims have specified form requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office recognizes dependent claims, multiple dependent claims, and claims in dependent form subject to the statutory and formal requirements (see 1.75(b), 1.75(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must show every feature and be described in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings: Must be described in and referred to specification; Must show every feature of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drawings are necessary for understanding the invention, they must be part of the application, be described in and referenced by the specification, and show all features of the invention (see 1.81, 1.83).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for drawings (format and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for drawings: size of sheet and margins; character of lines; hatching and shading; lead lines; legends; letters; reference characters; scale; symbols; views; numbering of sheets and views; arrows; holes; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings must conform to the Office drawing standards (paper, margins, ink, scale, hatching, shading, legends, reference characters, numbering, views, symbols, arrows, lead lines and other requirements) and are governed by the drawing rules listed at 1.84 and related subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original drawings retention and release prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Original should be retained by applicant; Release not permitted; No return or release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should retain original drawings and originals generally will not be returned or released by the Office (see 1.81(a), 1.85(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper, writing, and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Language, paper, writing, margin: application papers must conform to prescribed paper and writing standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must meet the Office's physical paper and writing standards (language, margins, etc.) as specified in the rules (see 1.52 and related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference in specification is permitted under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large tables, sequence listings, and other material may be incorporated by reference in compliance with the Office rules (see 1.52(e) and sections on electronic documents, 1.58, 1.96, and sequence listing rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of biological material requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit of biological material: acceptable depository, biological material, examination procedures, furnishing of samples, need/opportunity to make a deposit, replacement or supplemental deposit, term of deposit, time of making original deposit, viability of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosure requires biological material for enablement, deposits must be made to an acceptable depository and meet requirements for viability, timing, replacement, examination procedure, furnishing of samples, and term as described in the deposit rules (see 1.801–1.809 and related subsections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure (information disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty of disclosure: Applicants have a duty of disclosure (to disclose known relevant information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and practitioners must comply with the duty of disclosure, ensuring submission of known material information (see 1.56 and 1.555 for reexamination-related duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and oath requirements; substitute statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration (oath) requirements: in patent application; foreign language declarations; in lieu of oath; substitute statement permitted under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath/declaration rules (including foreign-language declarations and substitute statements) govern who signs, acceptable formats, and when substitute statements are appropriate (see 1.64–1.69 and related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application parts and filing: parts desirably filed together; parts of complete application
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of application desirably filed together; parts of complete application: which parts constitute a complete application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised what parts should be filed together and what constitutes parts of a complete application (see 1.51 and 1.54 for filing of parts and their desirable contemporaneous submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification required in letters concerning application or patent (identify application/patent in correspondence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence with the Office must identify the relevant application or patent clearly in accordance with identification rules (see 1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies, records, and public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of patents, published applications, records, etc., and records open to public inspection; document supply fees and orders for copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public and applicant access to Office records, procedures for ordering copies, fees for copies, and public inspection rules are specified and must be followed (see 1.11–1.13, 1.19, 1.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic document submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic documents: application size fee; optical/compact disc submissions; sequence listings; computer program listing appendix; large tables — requirements when submitted as part of the permanent record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions must comply with the Office electronic submission rules (application size fees, format requirements for sequence listings, program listings, large tables, optical disc rules) and incorporation by reference rules (see 1.16(s), 1.52(f), 1.96, 1.821–1.834).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims rejection and examination completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection of claims; completeness of examiner’s action; reasons for allowance; citation of references; examiner’s action as to form and substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination includes form and substantive review; examiners must cite references and provide reasons for allowance or rejection; the completeness of the examiner’s action and proper citation are governed by 1.104 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority, effective filing date, and related filing-date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective filing date of a claimed invention and related filing date/priority rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules determine effective filing dates for claims (under AIA and pre-AIA rules), priority claims, and related consequences for patentability (see 1.109 and related provisions).
